approved_scope.title: Finalize, ship and archive refuse an approvals ledger that Git history does not hold
approved_scope.description: finalize, ship and archive refuse an approvals ledger that Git history does not hold
acceptance_criteria: An accepted change archives with the closing records its accepting step wrote and has not committed, and no other uncommitted approval.

Every rewrite the tool itself makes still finalizes: a reopen, a send-back and fresh approval, a relay restored or removed by `change repair-relays` in an approval or in the approval a reopening embeds, the reopening members `specsync migrate 5.0` backfills, and a ledger member this version does not know.
The usual flow, approve, `check --commit`, review and finalize, archives as before.

They refuse when a committed version of the ledger rewrites or drops an earlier approval, reopening or send-back, naming the commit that did it, the commit before it and the record; that covers a change deleted and created again under the same id, and a record an older SpecSync rewrote without a member it did not know.

`change finalize`, `change ship` and `change archive` refuse, writing nothing, a change whose `approvals.json` is not committed at `HEAD` or differs from the committed version, naming the file and the way out: the commit when the working copy only adds records, the restore when it changes a committed one.
`change ship-status` lists the refusal as a blocker and does not report the change ready, and `change ship --dry-run` refuses with it.

applied_items.content:
`change finalize`, `change ship` and `change archive` SHALL archive only an approvals ledger that Git history holds. Before any of them writes, the change's `approvals.json` SHALL be committed at `HEAD` and the working copy SHALL equal that committed version. For a change that is already `accepted`, the working copy MAY add, after the records committed at `HEAD`, only the closing records its accepting step wrote and has not committed: the one `finalization` approval of a finalization that stopped before the archive move, or the `acceptance` approval of `change accept` and the normalizing `definition` approval it may write before it. Every committed version of the ledger along the first-parent history of `HEAD` SHALL extend the version committed before it: each record of `approvals`, `reopenings` and `send_backs` SHALL stay at its position, unchanged. Two differences SHALL NOT count as a change: the `relayed_by` of an approval, whether that approval is a record of `approvals` or the `superseded_approval` a record of `reopenings` embeds, which `change repair-relays` restores or removes; and the `stale_acceptance_input_digest` and `current_acceptance_input_digest` members `specsync migrate 5.0` adds to a reopening that lacked them. A commit that removed the ledger, as an archive move removes it, SHALL be skipped, so the version committed after it is compared with the last one committed before it; a change that was removed and created again under the same id, other than by an archive and a reopen, therefore SHALL be refused. Members of the ledger other than those three lists SHALL NOT be compared. A refusal SHALL be made before anything is written and SHALL name the file and the way out. When the working copy only adds records to the version at `HEAD`, or the file is not committed at all, the way out is to commit it, which `specsync change check <id> --commit` does. When the working copy changes or drops a committed record, it is `git checkout HEAD -- <path>`. For a committed rewrite, the refusal SHALL name the commit that made it, the commit it rewrote and the record; and because a commit already in history cannot be made to extend the one before it, it SHALL say the two ways out: take the rewriting commit out of the branch's history, or make the change again under a new id.

Acceptance Criteria
- After review, with one approval's actor rewritten in the working tree, `change finalize` and `change ship` refuse, name `approvals.json`, `HEAD` and the restore, and archive nothing; restoring the file lets the same command archive.
- With that rewrite committed before verification and review, they refuse and name the commit that rewrote the ledger; a dropped approval, a rewritten reopening and a dropped send-back are refused the same way.
- A ledger that was never committed is refused, and so is one whose working copy only adds records the tool wrote, as after `change reopen` and a plain `change check` with nothing committed; both name the commit as the way out, never the restore, which would drop those records.
- A change whose workspace was deleted in one commit and created again under the same id in a later one is refused, naming the commit that last held the earlier ledger and the two ways out. A change reopened out of its archive is not: its ledger extends the last one committed before the archive move.
- A committed version in which an older SpecSync dropped a member of an earlier record is refused like any other rewrite, with the same two ways out; a dropped `relayed_by`, the member 6.2.0 and older are known to drop, is not compared and passes, in an approval and in the approval a reopening embeds.
- Each of these still finalizes: a change reopened and verified again; a change sent back and approved again; a relay committed and then removed, and one restored, as `change repair-relays` does, in an approval and in the `superseded_approval` of a reopening; a reopening that gains the two digest members `specsync migrate 5.0` adds; and a ledger that gains a member this version does not know.
- An accepted change archives with the closing records `change accept` wrote and has not committed, and a finalization that stopped after acceptance resumes; an accepted change whose working copy adds any other approval, or changes a committed one, is refused.
- A rewrite made on a branch that was merged in is refused at the merge commit that brought it onto the first-parent history.
- The usual flow (approve, `check --commit`, review, finalize) archives as before.

`change ship-status` SHALL list the refusal of REQ-change-166 as a blocker, with the same message, and SHALL NOT report the change ready to finalize while it holds. `change ship --dry-run` SHALL refuse with that message.

Acceptance Criteria
- With one approval's actor rewritten in the working tree after review, `change ship-status <id>` lists the blocker, reports `ready_to_finalize` false and exits 1, and `change ship <id> --dry-run` refuses with the same message.
- With the file restored, `ready_to_finalize` is true again.
